segments.text: This video was not edited. An agent wrote it, and the machine it is playing on rendered it.
Making an explainer normally costs an afternoon. You write the script, record it twice, then drag clips around a timeline until the words finally line up with the pictures.
Xplainer gives your coding agent five tools. It creates the video, writes the scenes as real code, narrates them, checks a frame, and renders. You only ask for the video.

The trick is the order. The speech is generated first, with a timestamp on every single word, so every scene length is measured instead of guessed, and the captions are already in sync before one frame has been drawn.
Which makes it cheap to explain the things you would never have filmed. A pull request. A new hire's first week. Last night's outage. The architecture that only two people understand.
Setting it up is three commands. Install the tool, let it fetch a browser and a voice, then connect your agent. Claude Code and Codex both work.
Nothing is uploaded, nothing is rendered anywhere but your own machine, and all of it is open source. Go and ask your agent for a video.
